text: {"frames":["Luuk the ferrywoman has not said a word since the fog came, so she taps the rail of her boat twice instead of answering you. On the deck lies a wheel of cheese cut into 12 equal slices, and the lock-keeper will let the boat through only when exactly half of it sits on the wooden tray. The canal under the Tower has begun to rise, and the water slaps higher against the hull with every breath of wind. You lean over the rail and watch the fog thin out over the water. How many slices make half of the wheel?","A cat named Marijke sits on the mill stair and refuses to move until the cheese is shared out, and she counts every step you take with her tail. The cheese-maker's wheel has been cut into 12 equal slices, and the baker's boy is waiting at the bottom with a basket. Marijke has decided that he may take only the share that makes half of the wheel, and not one slice more. The windmill sails above you creak as if they are listening too. How many slices make half of the wheel?","Behind the linen cupboard someone hums the old song about the windmill, and the humming stops whenever you move your hand. You pull out the drawer and find a wheel of cheese cut into 12 equal slices, wrapped in a tea towel that smells of tulips. The humming starts again, softer, and it comes from the wardrobe next to the cupboard. You fold the tea towel back over the cheese and slide the drawer shut without a sound. How many slices make half of the wheel?","Give me half of your cheese and I will tell you which stair in the Tower is the true one, says Alfie, the boy who can hear the water under the floors. You look at the wheel on the bench, cut into 12 equal slices, and the stair you need is still hidden. Alfie presses his ear to the floorboards and nods, because the water tells him the stair is waiting for the right share. The bargain is open and the cheese is in your hands. How many slices make half of the wheel?","Someone has laid every tulip in the field into a pattern overnight, and the neighbours across the dyke are shouting that the pattern is theirs. Briony, who collects fog in jars, has come to the dyke with a wheel of cheese cut into 12 equal slices as the prize for whoever wins. She sets the wheel on a stump and says that each side must get its fair share, which is exactly half of the wheel. The neighbours go quiet and look at the slices, then at the tulips, then at you. How many slices make half of the wheel?"]}
